titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§211–213: Jelme, Tolun and Önggür
about: Chinggis continues the rewards of 1206. He recalls how Jelme and his father came down to the Onan at his birth and was his bondman from the cradle, forgiving him nine offences; makes Tolun a cherbi for gathering his people; and rewards Önggür the cook, who asks for his Baja'ud kinsmen and is given a thousand, then fixes how Önggür and Boroqul are to serve the feast and how the guests are to be seated.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Želme-de ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, to Jelme saying:
sentences.n: The colon after ügülerün opens the speech, which is about Jelme. The Ming gives Želme-de its 行, ‘to’, yet the speech then talks of Jelme in the third person; whether he is addressed with others present or spoken of, the Ming does not say, so the translation keeps ‘to’. ügülerün is ügüle- ‘to speak’ with the converb of time -rün, ‘when saying’; Čiṅgis Qaγan is name plus title.
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Jelme:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Žarčiγ̇udai ebügen kürege-ben ürču Želme ölegei-te-eče
sentences.l: "Žarčiγ̇udai old-man bellows-his-own carrying, Želme cradle-from
sentences.n: The speech begins; Shiratori’s opening quotation mark is on Žarčiγ̇udai, and the closing mark comes at orotuγai. The sentence is long and runs on through the next two units. Žarčiγ̇udai is the smith-father of Jelme (kürege, Ming 風匣 ‘wind box’, is the bellows). ürču is ür- ‘carry on the back’ plus the converb -ču, the stem inferred from the Ming 背着; -ben is the reflexive-possessive ‘his own’. ölegei-te-eče (Ming 搖車 自的行, ‘cradle … from’) ends in the ablative -eče, but the -te- before it is not accounted for and the Ming does not show it; I read ‘from the cradle’, i.e. from earliest childhood. Whether Jelme was carried in a cradle or merely came ‘from his cradle’ is not settled by these words; the sentence has no verb until büleġei, three units on.
sentences.i: “The old man Jarchiudai, carrying his bellows on his back, and Jelme, from his cradle,

morph.gloss: to carry on the back (stem inferred from the Ming) [背着]
uncertain element between stem and ablative; not shown in the Ming

sentences.t: Burqan-Qaldun-ača baγ̇užu irerün Onan-(n)u Deliġün-Boldaγ-a nama-ji töreküi-dür
sentences.l: Burqan-Qaldun-from descending, coming-when, Onan’s Deliġün-Boldaγ-at, me at-being-born,
sentences.n: A converb chain: baγ̇užu (baγu- ‘come down’ + -žu), irerün (ire- ‘come’ + -rün, ‘when coming’), then the time clause nama-ji töreküi-dür, ‘at (my) being born’ (töre- ‘be born’ + participle -küi + dative-locative -dür). The ablative Burqan-Qaldun-ača has the Ming 行, ‘to’, though the form is ‘from’; I follow the form. Deliġün-Boldaγ-a is the place with the dative-locative -a (Ming 行). nama-ji is the oblique stem of bi ‘I’ with an accusative -ji, so ‘me’, not ‘my’; the reading ‘at my birth’ is the sense of the whole clause. The Onan is Shiratori’s spelling of the Onon.
sentences.i: when they came down from Burqan Qaldun to Deligün-Boldaq on the Onan, at my birth,

morph.gloss: ablative: from (the Ming has 行, its usual dative marker, but the form is ablative) [行]
the Onan (Onon), river of the homeland [河名]

sentences.t: buluγan nelke ögčü büleġei.
sentences.l: sable swaddling-cloth giving was.
sentences.n: The main verb of the sentence begun two units back: ögčü (ög- ‘give’ + -ču) büleġei (bü- ‘be’ + past -leġei), a converb plus ‘was’, a past habitual or perfect. The subject is Jarchiudai, as the long sentence is built, but he is never named again, so ‘he’ is my inference. nelke is Ming 褯衣, a baby’s wrapping; buluγan is ‘sable’ (貂鼠).
sentences.i: he gave me swaddling-clothes of sable.

morph.gloss: swaddling-cloth (Ming 褯衣, a baby wrap) [褯衣]

sentences.t: Tere nököčegšeġer bosoγa-jin boγ̇ol egüden-ü emčü bolba-že.
sentences.l: That companion-since threshold’s bondman, door’s own became indeed.
sentences.n: bolba-že is bol- ‘become’ + past -ba + -že, ‘indeed’ (Ming 做了 也者︀). nököčegšeġer has the Ming 倣伴以來, ‘since being companions’; I read the stem nököče- ‘companion’ with an ending -šeġer, ‘ever since’, but the split is uncertain. boγ̇ol is ‘bondman’; bosoγa-jin ‘of the threshold’ (Ming 門限); egüden-ü ‘of the door’ (Ming 門子的, which can also mean a doorkeeper); emčü, Ming 梯已 ‘own, private’, makes him a personal servant. The subject is Jelme; he is not named in the unit, so the pronoun is from context.
sentences.i: From that companionship on, he became a bondman of the threshold, a private servant of the door.

morph.gloss: to be a companion (stem uncertain) [倣伴以來]
'ever since' (ending uncertain; the Ming 以來 'since')
door (Ming 門子, which can also mean a doorkeeper) [門子]

sentences.t: Želme-jin tusa in-ü olon bi-že.
sentences.l: Želme’s service his many is indeed.
sentences.n: tusa is Ming 恩, ‘favour’, here a service rendered. in-ü is the third-person genitive set after its noun, ‘his’, the Ming 他的; the Mongol repeats the owner (‘Jelme’s service, his’). bi-že is the verb ‘to be’, in its stem bi- before the particle -že, ‘indeed’.
sentences.i: Jelme’s services are many.

morph.gloss: his (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.t: Töreküi-lüġe töreldügsen öšküi-lüġe ösülčegsen
sentences.l: Born-at together born, growing-at together grown,
sentences.n: Four forms in a parallel pair: töreküi-lüġe ‘at birth together’ (Ming 生時 一同; the -lüġe is the comitative), töreldügsen ‘born together’ (Ming 共生了的; reciprocal-collective -ldü- ‘together’ + participle -gsen), then the same for ‘grow’: öšküi-lüġe, ösülčegsen. The speaker presumably means Jelme and himself, but the words do not say ‘I’ or ‘we’, so the translation leaves the pair unnamed.
sentences.i: Born together at birth, grown together at growth,

morph.gloss: to be born [生時 一同]

sentences.t: buluγan nelke hužaγ̇urtu ölžetü qutuγtu Želme
sentences.l: Sable swaddling-cloth root-having, fortune-having, blessing-having Želme
sentences.n: Three words in -tu/-tü, ‘having’ (the possessive pattern): hužaγ̇urtu ‘having a root’ (Ming 根源), ölžetü ‘having fortune’ (Ming 福︀), qutuγtu ‘having blessing’ (Ming 慶). Jelme is named last, as the thing they all describe. Which noun the ‘root’ belongs to is my reading: the Ming puts ‘sable swaddling-cloth’ before 根源, so I take the sable wrappings as the root of Jelme’s standing. That reading is tentative.
sentences.i: Jelme, who has the sable swaddling-clothes as his root, the fortunate, the blessed,

sentences.t: jesün aldal aldaγ̇asu ereġü-dür bu orotuγai"
sentences.l: nine fault if-incurring, guilt-in not let-enter"
sentences.n: Shiratori’s closing quotation mark is on orotuγai. jesün is ‘nine’ with the Ming 九次, ‘nine times’. aldal is Ming 罰 ‘penalty’, then alda- with the conditional -γ̇asu (Ming 罰呵); I take aldal alda- as ‘to incur a penalty’, a noun-and-verb pair. ereġü-dür is ‘in guilt’ (Ming 罪裏). bu orotuγai is the prohibitive bu with the third-person optative -tuγai; the Ming 敎入者︀ has ‘cause to enter’, so ‘let no one bring him into guilt’ is the closer sense. The exact force of ‘nine’ (nine offences pardoned) is my reading from the Ming; the words do not say ‘pardoned’.
sentences.i: if he offends nine times, let him not be brought to guilt for it.”

morph.gloss: to incur a penalty, be at fault (Ming 罰, ‘punish’; sense uncertain) [罰呵]

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.n: keġen is the converb of keġe- ‘say’ that closes a quotation (Ming 麽道). žarliγ bolba, ‘became a decree’, is the formula for issuing one; both are as elsewhere in the text.
sentences.i: So saying, he issued a decree.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Tolun-a ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, to Tolun saying:
sentences.n: Shiratori prints the name as Tolun-a, the dative -a (Ming 人名 行, ‘to’). He is the Tolun of the seating in §213 (Tolum-tan-luγ̇a), and the holder of the cherbi title given here; the Mongol does not say so, it is my identification from the name.
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Tolun:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Tolun, a man's name (Shiratori prints Tolun-a) [人名]

sentences.t: "Ečige köġün öġere miṅγa ker medekü büleġe či.
sentences.l: "Father, son apart, thousand how to-manage was you.
sentences.n: This is the hardest sentence of §212. The Ming runs: 父 子 𠮠 千 怎 管的 有來 你, ‘father, son, apart, thousand, how, manage, was, you’. I take ečige köġün öġere as ‘father and son apart’ (öġere ‘other, apart’, Ming 𠮠), and medekü büleġe as ‘was managing’, with ker ‘how’ (Ming 怎). Whether the sense is a question (‘how could you manage…’) or a statement about what Tolun once did is uncertain; the opening quotation mark is on Ečige (Shiratori) and closes at či below.
sentences.i: “As father and son apart, how was it that you managed a thousand?

sentences.t: Ulus qurijaldun ečige-dēče öröle žiġür bolun
sentences.l: People gathering, father-from single wing becoming,
sentences.n: qurijaldun is qurija- ‘gather’ (stem inferred from the Ming 收集) with the reciprocal-collective -ldu- and a converb -n (Ming 共收集, ‘gather together’). ečige-dēče is ‘from the father’ (ablative, written with long ē; Ming 父行). öröle has only the Ming 隻, ‘single’; I guess ‘alone, on one’s own’ but the word is not otherwise known to me, so the rendering ‘apart’ is uncertain. žiġür is ‘wing’ (Ming 翅); bolun ‘becoming’. The figure of the wing is the Mongol’s, not an addition.
sentences.i: Gathering the people, you became a wing apart from your father,

morph.gloss: to gather (stem inferred from the Ming) [共收集]
single, alone (sense uncertain; the Ming has only 隻, ‘single, one of a pair’) [隻]

sentences.t: žigtüldüžü ulus qurijalduγsan tula čerbi nere ögbe-že.
sentences.l: Pulling together, people having-gathered because-of, cherbi title gave indeed.
sentences.n: žigtüldüžü has the Ming 共拽着, ‘pulling together’; I give it žigtü- ‘pull’ + -ldü- ‘together’ + -žü, but the stem is inferred from the Ming and the analysis is uncertain. qurijalduγsan is the past participle ‘having gathered’, followed by tula ‘because of’ (Ming 上頭). čerbi is an office, its meaning not known (Ming 官名); nere is ‘name, title, rank’. ögbe-že is ög- ‘give’ + past -be + ‘indeed’. The unit carries on the converb chain from the one before.
sentences.i: Pulling together, and because you had gathered the people, I gave you the title of cherbi.

morph.gloss: to pull, drag (stem inferred from the Ming 拽; analysis uncertain) [共拽着]
because of, on account of [上頭]
cherbi, an office or rank (meaning not known) [官名]

sentences.t: Edöġe öġer-ün oluγsan žüġegsen(i)-jer(i)-jen öġer-ün miṅγa bolžu
sentences.l: Now own-obtained, own-set-with-his own, own thousand becoming,
sentences.n: edöġe ‘now’ (Ming 如今). öġer-ün oluγsan is ‘the own, obtained’ (öġer ‘own’, ablative-genitive -ün; olu- ‘obtain’ + -γsan). žüġegsen(i)-jer(i)-jen is a heavy form: žüġe- ‘set, place’ (Ming 置, stem inferred) + -gsen + linking (i) + the instrumental -jer ‘with’ (Ming 敎) + (i) + the reflexive-possessive -jen ‘one’s own’. I take it as ‘with those you set in place’. The converb bolžu ‘becoming’ (Ming 做着) closes the unit, which has no finite verb of its own; it leads into the question that follows. The reading as a whole is tentative.
sentences.i: Now, with those you yourself obtained and those you set up as your own, making a thousand of your own,

morph.gloss: to set, place, establish (Ming 置; stem inferred) [置來的]
instrumental: with (Shiratori's (i) is a linking vowel) [敎]

sentences.t: Turuqan-dur ejetüldüžü ülü-ü aqu či"
sentences.l: Turuqan-with consulting-together, not-? stay you"
sentences.n: Closing quotation mark at či. Turuqan-dur is the name with the dative-locative -dur (Ming 行, ‘to, with’); ejetüldüžü is Ming 商量着, ‘consulting’, from eje- ‘counsel’ (see §§204–207) with the reciprocal -ldü- and the converb -žü. ülü-ü is ülü ‘not’ with a final -ü, probably the question particle; the Ming gives 不 on ülü and 麽 (the question mark) with aqu. aqu is a- ‘stay, be’ with the participle -qu. So ‘won’t you stay, consulting with Turuqan?’ — a question by form, probably a command by force. Who Turuqan is, the Mongol does not say.
sentences.i: Will you not stay and consult with Turuqan?”

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.n: The closing formula: keġen žarliγ bolba, as in §211.
sentences.i: So saying, he issued a decree.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Öṅgür, baγ̇urči-da ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, Önggür, to-the-cook saying:
sentences.n: Shiratori’s comma after Öṅgür separates the name from baγ̇urči-da, ‘to the cook’ (Ming 厨子 行); I read them as one person, ‘to Önggür, the cook’. ügülerün is the converb of time ‘when saying’; the colon introduces the speech.
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Önggür, the cook:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Γurban Toquraγ̇ud tabun Tarqud Möṅgetü-Kijan-u köġü
sentences.l: "Three Toquraγ̇ud, five Tarqud, Möṅgetü-Kijan’s son
sentences.n: The opening quotation mark is on Γurban; Chinggis’s speech runs to či below. γurban ‘three’ and tabun ‘five’ are followed by two clan names (Ming 姓 ‘surname, clan’), then ‘Mönggetü-Kiyan’s son’ (köġü, a short form of köġün). I take the two clan groups as a description of the father’s people and ‘son’ as the person addressed. The grouping of the numbers with Mönggetü-Kiyan is my reading, not shown by the Ming, which runs the words together.
sentences.i: “Mönggetü-Kiyan’s son, of the three Toquraud and five Tarqud,

sentences.t: či Öṅgür, Bišiγ̇ud, Bajaγ̇ud(i)-jar ta na-dur nigen küreġen bolžu
sentences.l: you Önggür, Bišiγ̇ud, with-Bajaγ̇ud you me-to one circle becoming,
sentences.n: či Öṅgür, Bišiγ̇ud, is probably ‘you, Önggür, a Bishi’ud’ (the comma sets Bišiγ̇ud in apposition). Bajaγ̇ud(i)-jar is the clan name with the instrumental -jar ‘with’ (Ming 敎); Shiratori’s bracketed (i) is a linking vowel. ta is the plural polite ‘you’, so the sentence has a plural subject, Önggür and his people. na-dur is bi ‘I’ (oblique stem na-) with -dur ‘to’ (Ming 我行). nigen küreġen is ‘one ring’ (Ming 圈子, a circle camp, the ring of tents), bolžu ‘becoming’. The sense ‘around me’ is my inference from na-dur; the Ming says only ‘to me’.
sentences.i: you, Önggür, a Bishi’ud, together with the Baja’ud, you formed a single ring around me,

morph.gloss: instrumental: with (Shiratori's (i) is a linking vowel) [敎]
ring of tents, circle camp [圈子]

sentences.t: či Öṅgür budan-dur ese toγ̇oriba-že či.
sentences.l: you Önggür fog-in not lost indeed you.
sentences.n: toγ̇oriba-že is toγ̇ori- ‘go astray’ (stem inferred from the Ming 迷, ‘lost’) + past -ba + -že. ese is the negative of past actions (Ming 不曾). budan-dur is ‘in fog’ (Ming 霧 裏). The fog is a figure for confusion or hard times; the Mongol does not explain it.
sentences.i: You, Önggür, did not lose your way in the fog.

morph.gloss: to get lost, go astray (stem inferred from the Ming) [迷了也者︀]

sentences.t: Bulγa-dur ese qaγačaba-že či.
sentences.l: Turmoil-in not parted indeed you.
sentences.n: Bulγa-dur: bulγa is Ming 反亂, ‘rebellion, disorder’, with -dur ‘in’; Shiratori’s capital is at the start of a sentence, not a name. qaγačaba-že is qaγača- ‘part, separate’ + past -ba + -že (Ming 離了 也者︀). The wording ‘did not part’ suggests ‘did not desert me’, but the Mongol has no object.
sentences.i: You did not leave in the turmoil.

morph.gloss: to part, leave, be separated [離了也者︀]

sentences.t: Noitan nobšildužü köiten köbšildüžü jabuba-že či.
sentences.l: Wet being-wet-together, cold being-cold-together, went indeed you.
sentences.n: noitan ‘wet’ (Ming 濕) and köiten ‘cold’ (Ming 寒; see the §§204–207 note) are each followed by a form in -ldu-/-ldü- ‘together’ with the converb ending: nobšildužü ‘being wet together’ (Ming 共濕着), köbšildüžü ‘being cold together’ (Ming 共寒着). The stems nobši-, köbši- are inferred from the Ming and their relation to the adjectives is uncertain. jabuba-že is jabu- ‘go’ + past + -že, ‘went on’, a figure for sharing hardship.
sentences.i: Wet together, cold together, you went on.

morph.gloss: to be wet (from noitan; stem inferred from the Ming) [共濕着]
to be cold (stem inferred from the Ming) [共寒着]
to walk, go [行了 也者︀]

sentences.t: Edöġe ambar sojurγal abqu či" keġeġesü
sentences.l: Now what favour to-take you" saying-if,
sentences.n: Shiratori’s closing mark falls after či. The inner speech asks the favour; keġeġesü is keġe- ‘say’ with the conditional -ġesü, ‘if, when (he) says’ (Ming 說呵). ambar ‘what’ (Ming 甚麽) is a rare word whose sense is only as the Ming has it. abqu is ab- ‘take’ + the participle -qu (Ming 要). This closes the speech that opened at Γurban, several units back.
sentences.i: Now what favour will you take?” When he said this,

sentences.t: Öṅgür ügülerün:
sentences.l: Önggür saying:
sentences.n: Önggür replies. ügülerün as above; the quotation mark opens at Sojurγal in the next unit.
sentences.i: Önggür said:

sentences.t: "Sojurγal soγ̇oṅγuluγ̇asu Bajaγ̇ud aqa deġü min-u qari qari tutum-dur bura tara bi.
sentences.l: "Favour if-let-choose, Bajaγ̇ud elder-brothers younger-brothers my, tribe tribe in-each scattered dispersed are.
sentences.n: Shiratori’s opening quotation mark is on Sojurγal. soγ̇oṅγuluγ̇asu has the Ming 敎揀呵, ‘if one lets (me) choose’; I read soγ̇oṅγul- ‘choose’ with a causative sense and the conditional -uγ̇asu, but the stem is inferred from the Ming. aqa deġü ‘elder and younger brothers’ is the usual pairing for kinsmen, here the Baja’ud clan; min-u ‘my’ follows. qari qari is Ming 部落 部落, ‘tribe, tribe’, doubled; tutum-dur I take as ‘in each’ (tutum, Ming 每, ‘each, every’; the sense is uncertain). bura tara are two near-rhyming words, ‘scattered, dispersed’ (Ming 漫 散). bi is ‘are’.
sentences.i: “If I am to choose a favour: my Baja’ud brothers, elder and younger, are scattered and dispersed, in tribe after tribe.

morph.gloss: to choose (stem inferred from the Ming 揀; the Ming 敎 'cause' suggests a causative) [敎揀呵]
each, every (sense uncertain; Ming 每) [每]

sentences.t: sojurγaγ̇asu Bajaγ̇ud aqa deġü-ġen čiγ̇ulγasuγai" keġeġesü
sentences.l: favour if-showing, Bajaγ̇ud elder-brothers younger-brothers-own let-me-gather" saying-if,
sentences.n: Closing quotation mark at čiγ̇ulγasuγai. sojurγaγ̇asu is sojurγa- ‘show favour’ with the conditional -γ̇asu (Ming 恩賜呵). čiγ̇ulγasuγai is čiγ̇ul- ‘gather’ (Ming 聚) + causative -γa- + the first-person optative -suγai (Ming 敎完聚我, ‘let me cause to gather’). deġü-ġen is ‘younger brother’ with the reflexive -ġen, ‘his own’, which sits oddly after the plural sense of aqa deġü; the Ming 弟自的行 shows it as ‘own’. keġeġesü closes it, ‘when he said’.
sentences.i: If you show me favour, let me gather my own Baja’ud brothers,” he said.

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow a grace [恩賜呵]
to gather, assemble (stem inferred from the Ming) [敎完聚我]

sentences.t: "Že tein Bajaγ̇ud aqa deġü-ġen čiγ̇ulγažu či mede miṅγan"
sentences.l: "So be it! Bajaγ̇ud elder-brothers younger-brothers-own having-gathered, you manage thousand"
sentences.n: Chinggis answers. že tein is ‘so be it, thus’ (že Ming 也者︀, tein Ming 那般). čiγ̇ulγažu is the causative converb of čiγ̇ul-, ‘making gather’ (Ming 敎完聚着), and mede is the bare stem of mede- ‘manage’ (Ming 管) as an imperative; miṅγan is ‘a thousand’ (Ming 千戶), the military unit. The translation turns the converb ‘gathering’ into an imperative ‘gather’; the Mongol has the second command only on mede.
sentences.i: “So be it. Gather your own Baja’ud brothers, and manage a thousand.”

morph.gloss: particle, 'so be it, very well' [也者︀]
to know, to manage (bare stem, imperative) [管]

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.n: The decree formula, as above.
sentences.i: So saying, he issued a decree.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan decree when-making:
sentences.n: žarliγ bolurun is the formula for ‘issued a decree’, with the converb of time -urun; the colon begins the decree.
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Öṅgür, Boroγ̇ul qojar baraγ̇un žeġün eteġed ta qojar baγ̇určin ideġen tügeġerün
sentences.l: "Önggür, Boroqul two, right left sides, you two cooks, food when-giving-out,
sentences.n: Shiratori’s opening quotation mark is on Öṅgür; it closes at tügeġedkün in the unit that ends the speech. The Ming reads 人名 人名 兩箇 右 左 邊 您 兩箇 厨子每 喫食 給散時. The two names are followed by qojar ‘two’ and then ‘right, left, sides’ (baraγ̇un žeġün eteġed, Ming 右 左 邊), and again ‘you two cooks’ (baγ̇určin with -n, Ming 每). I take the two cooks as the pair, one for each side, but the Mongol only lists the words. ideġen is ‘food’; tügeġe- ‘give out’ with -rün is ‘when giving out’. eteġed is ‘sides’ (Ming 邊); its stem is uncertain.
sentences.i: “Önggür and Boroqul, you two cooks of the right side and the left, when you give out the food,

morph.gloss: side, flank (stem uncertain; -d may be a plural or part of the stem) [邊]

sentences.t: baraγ̇un eteġed baiγsan saγ̇uγsan-a ülü dutaγ̇ulun
sentences.l: right side standing, to-sitting, not let-lack,
sentences.n: baiγsan is bai- ‘stand’ + -γsan, ‘those who stood’ (Ming 立(了)的); saγ̇uγsan-a is the same for saγ̇u- ‘sit’, with the dative -a on the second only (Ming 坐(了)的行). ülü dutaγ̇ulun is the negative ülü with dut- ‘lack’ + causative -aγ̇ul- + converb -un, ‘not letting lack’ (Ming 敎缺了). The contrast ‘standing / sitting’ is the Ming’s reading of the two participles.
sentences.i: do not let those who stand, or sit, on the right side go short,

sentences.t: žeġün eteġed žergelegsen esegsen-e ülü dutaγ̇ulun
sentences.l: left side ranked, to-those-who-have-not, not let-lack,
sentences.n: žeġün eteġed is the ‘left side’ (Ming 左 邊). žergelegsen is žergele- ‘line up, rank’ (žerge ‘row’, stem inferred from the Ming 列) + -gsen, ‘those lined up’ (Ming 列了的); esegsen-e (Ming 不曾的(行)) is ‘to those who have not’ (ese is the negative of past actions; the form with -gsen is irregular, analysis uncertain). The pair mirrors ‘standing / sitting’ on the right; I read it as ‘those in their rank and those not’. The same ülü dutaγ̇ulun follows.
sentences.i: and do not let those on the left side, those in rank and those not, go short.

morph.gloss: to line up, rank (stem inferred from the Ming 列; žerge ‘row’) [列了的]

sentences.t: ta qojar-i tein tügeġeġeü
sentences.l: you two-to so if-giving-out,
sentences.n: ta qojar-i: ta ‘you’ (plural polite) with qojar ‘two’ and -i, which the Ming (兩箇行) glosses like a dative. tein ‘so’ (Ming 那般). tügeġeġeü is tügeġe- ‘give out’ with a conditional ending written -ġeü, ‘if’ (Ming 呵); the ending is probably a variant or slip for -ġesü and is left as printed.
sentences.i: If you two give out the food so,

morph.gloss: accusative or dative-like: ‘the two’ (the Ming 行)
conditional (as printed; perhaps a variant of -ġesü; Ming 呵)

sentences.t: min-u qoγ̇olai ülü qučin sedkil amuju.
sentences.l: my throat not choking, heart at-ease is.
sentences.n: The result clause. qoγ̇olai ‘throat’ (Ming 喉嚨); ülü qučin is ‘not choking’ (Ming 澁噎, ‘rough and choked’), the form qučin being unclear (a noun or a verb stem). sedkil ‘heart, mind’ (Ming 心). amuju is amu- ‘be at rest’ + -ju, a converb form used as the main verb, ‘is at ease’ (Ming 安有); the analysis is uncertain. The idiom is that a host who feeds all his guests has an easy mind.
sentences.i: my throat will not choke, and my heart will be at ease.

morph.gloss: to choke, be hoarse (Ming 澁噎; form and class uncertain) [澁噎]
to be at rest, at ease [安有]
converb-form used as a main verb: ‘is …’ (analysis uncertain)

sentences.t: Edöġe Öṅgür, Boroγ̇ul qojar morilažu jabužu ideġe olon küġün-e tügeġedkün"
sentences.l: Now Önggür, Boroqul two mounting going food many persons-to give-out"
sentences.n: Closing quotation mark at tügeġedkün. morilažu is morin ‘horse’ + the verb-former -la- + -žu, ‘mounting’ (Ming 上馬着); jabužu ‘going’ (Ming 行着). The Ming for küġün-e is 人行 (‘to people’). tügeġedkün (Ming 給散您) is tügeġe- + -d- + -kün, a plural polite imperative, ‘(you two) give out’; the -d- and the whole ending are uncertain. qojar here is ‘the two of you’; olon küġün-e ‘to many persons’ names the recipients.
sentences.i: Now you two, Önggür and Boroqul, mount, go about, and give out food to many people.”

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.n: The decree formula, as above.
sentences.i: So saying, he issued a decree.

sentences.t: saγ̇uri saγ̇urun jeke tüsürge-jin baraγ̇un žeġün eteġed ideġe basaγ̇alažu saγ̇udqun.
sentences.l: Seat when-sitting, great feast’s right left sides, food judging, sit.
sentences.n: Shiratori omits the opening quotation mark here (the closing mark comes at saγ̇utuγai below); I supply it in the translation. saγ̇uri is Ming 坐位, ‘seat’; saγ̇urun ‘when sitting’; tüsürge-jin ‘of the feast’ (Ming 酒局, ‘wine bureau’; the sense is uncertain). basaγ̇alažu is Ming 知料着, ‘knowing and reckoning’; I translate ‘taking account of’, but the stem is inferred and the sense is uncertain: it may mean to judge portions or to mind the order. saγ̇udqun is saγ̇u- ‘sit’ + -d- + -qun, a plural polite imperative (Ming 坐您). A very uncertain unit.
sentences.i: “At the seating, at the great banquet, sit on the right and left sides, taking account of the food.

morph.gloss: banquet, drinking-party (Ming 酒局, ‘wine office’; sense uncertain) [酒局]
to judge, reckon, take account (Ming 知料; stem inferred) [知料着]

sentences.t: Tolum-tan-luγ̇a tüblen saγ̇utuγai"
sentences.l: Tolun and-the-like with, in-the-middle let-them-sit"
sentences.n: Closing quotation mark at saγ̇utuγai. Tolum-tan-luγ̇a is the name Tolun (written Tolum before t) with -tan ‘and the like’ (Ming 等) and the comitative -luγ̇a (Ming 一同); tüblen has the Ming 面北居中, ‘facing north, in the centre’, whose stem I cannot analyse. saγ̇utuγai is the third-person optative; the Ming adds 敎, ‘cause’, which the form does not show. Who ‘they’ are, the words do not say; the Ming implies Tolun’s group, not Önggür and Boroqul.
sentences.i: With Tolun and the rest, let them sit in the middle.”

morph.gloss: Tolun (printed Tolum before t), a man’s name [人名等]
in the middle, facing north (Ming 面北居中; form and stem uncertain) [面北居中]

sentences.t: keġen saγ̇urin žiγ̇ažu ögbe.
sentences.l: Saying, place-of-sitting telling gave.
sentences.n: keġen as above. saγ̇urin is ‘a place for sitting’ (Ming 坐位); žiγ̇ažu is žiγ̇a- ‘tell, announce’ (Ming 吿) + converb -žu; ögbe ‘gave’. I read žiγ̇ažu ögbe as ‘assigned by telling’, i.e. told each where to sit; the pairing of ‘tell’ and ‘give’ is unusual and tentative.
sentences.i: So saying, he told them their seats and assigned them.

morph.gloss: a place for sitting, a seat [坐位]
